_about: Measured size of wheelchair users seated in their own chairs, for the shoulder, door and knee-space checks. Only the values those checks use, copied from the paper's Tables 4 (women) and 5 (men), overall sample (manual and power together). Centimetres, as printed.
source: Paquet V, Feathers D. An anthropometric study of manual and powered wheelchair users. International Journal of Industrial Ergonomics 33 (2004) 191-204, Tables 2, 4 and 5. doi:10.1016/j.ergon.2003.10.003
sample: 121 adults (46 women, 75 men) in Buffalo, NY who use a wheelchair as their main way of getting around; 46% used power chairs (about 7% in the U.S.), so big chairs are over-represented. Measured sitting comfortably, arms on the armrests.

acromion_height_cm._definition: Floor to the top of the shoulder (acromion), seated in the chair (Table 2).

overall_breadth_cm._definition: Widest point of the person and chair together, side to side (Table 2).

knee_height_cm._definition: Floor to the top of the kneecap (suprapatella), seated in the chair (Table 2).
knee_height_cm._subgroup_note: Some subgroups print higher 95th percentiles (women in power chairs, right: 81.0; men in manual chairs, right: 85.7). Those groups are small; the overall sample is used.

ada_knee_clearance_source: ADA 2010 Standards 306.3.1: space under an element between 9 inches (230 mm) and 27 inches (685 mm) above the finish floor counts as knee clearance
